newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda February inflation falls to 4.9 percent.
newsitem.headline: Uganda February inflation falls to 4.9 percent.

text.p: Uganda's annual headline inflation fell to 4.9 percent in February from 6.0 percent in January, the Bank of Uganda (BOU), the central bank, said on Monday.
In a report, BOU said the drop in inflation reflected in large part an increase in food supply -- mainly in Kampala.
The bank's comments contrasted with warnings by senior Ugandan food officials of impending famine in the drought-hit eastern districts of the East African country.
Ugandan authorities have appealed for international relief supplies to meet the famine threat.
The bank reported that the annual underlying inflation also declined, to 3.2 percent from 5.4 percent in the same period.
Decreased were seen in the prices of beverages and tobacco, household and personal goods and transport and communication group indices in the period under review, the bank said.
